404 Media recently reported a vulnerability in the iCloud+ "Hide My Email" feature that allowed anyone to access a user's real email address. Apple now says the issue has been officially fixed.

Apple says the security flaw in "Hide My Email" was patched earlier this month

If you're an iCloud+ or Apple One subscriber, Apple's "Hide My Email" privacy feature is particularly useful for protecting your real email address.

According to Apple's website, here's how it works:

However, according to a recent 404 Media report, "Hide My Email" has long had a vulnerability that could allow anyone to obtain the real email address linked to an Apple account. This disclosure has triggered a new proposed lawsuit.

Apple said today that the vulnerability has been officially patched earlier this month.

Apple told 404 Media that it "deployed a fix for this issue on July 3 and stated that the problem has been fully resolved."

The iCloud+ vulnerability was first reported to Apple by Tyler Murphy in June 2025. After an initial exchange, Apple claimed the flaw had been fixed, but Murphy found the issue still existed. Hopefully this time it's truly resolved.

How often do you use the "Hide My Email" feature on iCloud+? Feel free to share in the comments.
